ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r6.claim: People who assume descent from Abraham and Moses entitles them to Paradise are condemned; Islahi redirects attention to those prophets' teachings and sacrifices.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r6.anchor: Their attention is directed to the teachings and sacrifices of these prophets

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p65/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p65/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p65/r4.claim: The primary addressees are Quraysh and, secondarily, the People of the Book: the latter claimed Moses and Abraham, while Quraysh treated Abraham as ancestor and religious leader.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p65/r4.anchor: the addressees here are primarily the Quraysh and secondarily the People of the Book.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p65/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p65/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p65/r5.claim: Abraham is called one who fulfilled: he obeyed every divine directive, kept his promise, and passed every trial; 2:124 likewise says he fulfilled his test.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p65/r5.anchor: fulfilled his promise and who passed every test and trial in an outstanding way.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p65/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p65/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p65/r6.claim: Abraham’s high standing came from complete obedience and faithfulness, whereas his descendants seek his favor without obeying God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p65/r6.anchor: the high status achieved by Abraham (sws) in this world and in the next was the result of showing complete obedience and faithfulness to God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p66/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p66/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p66/r1.claim: If “scriptures of Abraham” denotes texts preserving his teachings, the attribution remains correct even if later exegesis appears in them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p66/r1.anchor: if by the scriptures of Abraham (sws) the reference is to the ones in which his teachings are mentioned

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r7.claim: “And Abraham” means the scriptures revealed to Abraham; the two prophets are singled out for a reported historical reason about who could be held responsible for others' crimes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r7.anchor: وإبراهيم: أي وفي صحف إبراهيم التي أنزلت عليه، وخص هذين النبيين عليهما أفضل الصلاة والسلام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r8.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r8.claim: One explanation says people between Noah and Abraham punished a person for the crimes of relatives and dependants; Abraham first opposed this, and from his law through Moses people were not held for another's crime.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r8.anchor: قيل: لأنه ما بين نوح وإبراهيم كانوا يأخذون الرجل بأبيه وابنه وعمه وخاله، والزوج بامرأته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r9.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r9.claim: The majority read waffā with a doubled fāʾ.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r10.speaker: أبو أمامة الباهلي وسعيد بن جبير وأبو مالك الغفاري وابن السميفع وزيد بن علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r10.claim: These readers recite waffā with a light fāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r10.anchor: وقرأ أبو أمامة الباهلي وسعيد بن جبير وأبو مالك الغفاري وابن السميفع وزيد بن علي: بتخفيفها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r11.claim: The object of “fulfilled” is left unstated so that it can include every kind of fulfillment, including conveying the message, bearing its burdens, patience in trials, and hospitality.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r11.anchor: ولم يذكر متعلق وفى ليتناول كل ما يصلح أن يكون متعلقا له، كتبليغ الرسالة والاستقلال بأعباء الرسالة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r12.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r12.claim: Al-Hasan says Abraham fulfilled everything God commanded him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r12.anchor: وعن الحسن: ما أمره الله بشيء إلا وفى به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r13.speaker: عطاء بن السائب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r13.claim: ʿAta ibn al-Saʾib says Abraham pledged not to ask a created being for anything.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r13.anchor: وعن عطاء بن السائب: عهد أن لا يسأل مخلوقا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r14.speaker: ابن عباس والربيع
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r14.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Rabiʿ say Abraham fulfilled obedience to God in the command to sacrifice his son.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r14.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والربيع: وفى طاعة الله في أمر ذبح ابنه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r15.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r15.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada say Abraham fulfilled the mission of conveying the message and striving for God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r15.anchor: وقال الحسن وقتادة: وفى بتبليغ الرسالة والمجاهدة في ذات الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r16.speaker: عكرمة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r16.claim: ʿIkrima identifies the ten verses beginning with “that no bearer bears another's burden” as what Abraham fulfilled.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r16.anchor: وقال عكرمة: وفي هذه العشر الآيات: ألا تزر فما بعدها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r17.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r17.claim: Ibn Abbas and Qatada say he fulfilled all obligatory obedience completely, perfected the branches of faith and Islam, and was thereby granted release from Hell.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r17.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا وقتادة: وفى ما افترض عليه من الطاعة على وجهها، وكملت له شعب الإيمان والإسلام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r18.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r18.claim: Ibn Abbas also says Abraham fulfilled thirty portions of Islamic law, ten each from al-Tawba, Qad aflaha, and al-Ahzab.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r18.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا: وفى شرائع الإسلام ثلاثين سهما، يعني: عشرة في براءة التائبون إلخ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r1.speaker: أبو أمامة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r1.claim: Abu Umama relates from the Prophet that Abraham's fulfillment included four prayers each day.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r1.anchor: وقال أبو أمامة: ورفعه إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، وفي أربع صلوات في كل يوم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r2.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r2.claim: Abu Bakr al-Warraq says Abraham fulfilled the claim he made when he answered God's command “Submit”; tests of his wealth, child, and self proved him faithful.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r2.anchor: وقال أبو بكر الوراق: قام بشرط ما ادعى، وذلك أن الله تعالى قال له: أسلم، قال: أسلمت لرب العالمين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r3.claim: The reported interpretations should be understood as examples of what Abraham fulfilled, not as an exhaustive definition.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r3.anchor: وينبغي أن تكون هذه الأقوال أمثلة لما وفى، لا على سبيل التعيين

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.claim: The third section calls people to reflect on their creation and transitions to enduring truths in the scriptures of Moses and Abraham.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.anchor: the third section (vv. 31–54) calls upon people to reflect upon their creation

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r17.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r17.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r17.claim: This section then turns to perennial truths attested in the scriptures of Moses and Abraham.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r17.anchor: transitions into a discussion of the perennial truths attested in the scriptures of Moses and Abraham

SAMIN-DURR:53:37/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:37/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:37/r1.anchor: إبراهيم }: عطف على " موسى " ، وإنما خص هذين النبيين عليهما السلام بالذكر

SAMIN-DURR:53:37/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:37/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:37/r2.claim: Abraham and Moses are singled out because between Abraham and Moses people were held liable for others’ offenses; Abraham first opposed this practice.
SAMIN-DURR:53:37/r2.anchor: لأنه كان بين إبراهيم وموسى يؤخذ الرجل بجريرة غيره، فأول من خالفهم إبراهيم عليه السلام.

SAMIN-DURR:53:37/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:37/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:37/r3.claim: أم is disconnected and means بل ألم ينبأ.
SAMIN-DURR:53:37/r3.anchor: " أم " منقطعة أي: بل ألم ينبأ.

SAMIN-DURR:53:37/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:37/r4.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:53:37/r4.claim: The common reading doubles the consonant in وفّى.

SAMIN-DURR:53:37/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:37/r5.speaker: أبو أمامة الباهلي وسعيد بن جبير وابن السميفع
SAMIN-DURR:53:37/r5.claim: Abū Umāma al-Bāhilī, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, and Ibn al-Sumayfa read وفى without doubling.
SAMIN-DURR:53:37/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو أمامة الباهلي وسعيد بن جبير وابن السميفع " وفى " مخففا.

SAMIN-DURR:53:37/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:37/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:37/r6.claim: The verb has three forms noted earlier; using both توفية and وفاء broadly includes all that Abraham fulfilled.
SAMIN-DURR:53:37/r6.anchor: وقد تقدم أن فيه ثلاث لغات، وأطلق التوفية والوفاء ليتناولا كل ما وفى.

QIRAAT-ER:53:37:2#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:53:37:2#1/r1.speaker: Lvw
QIRAAT-ER:53:37:2#1/r1.claim: The Lvw vocalization reads Ibrāhām instead of Ibrāhīm, replacing long ī with ā as a phonological adaptation of the foreign name; both are canonical.
QIRAAT-ER:53:37:2#1/r1.anchor: Variant vocalization: Ibrāhām instead of Ibrāhīm — the long ā replaces the long ī

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p251#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p251#2/r1.speaker: عمرو بن أوس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p251#2/r1.claim: ʿAmr ibn Aws says people were once held for another person's sin until Abraham came and God established that no bearer bears another's burden.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p251#2/r1.anchor: عن عمرو بن أوس في قوله تعالى ﴿ وإبراهيم الذي وفى ﴾ قال كان الرجل يؤخذ بذنب غيره حتى جاء إبراهيم

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p251#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p251#2/r2.speaker: ابن أبي نجيح
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p251#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abī Najīḥ glosses Abraham's fulfillment as carrying out what was required.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p251#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن أبي نجيح في قوله ﴿ وفي ﴾ أدى ﴿ ألا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى ﴾

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p251#2/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p251#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p251#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Kursī is the place of the two feet, while no one can measure the Throne.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p251#2/r4.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس قال الكرسي موضع القدمين والعرش لا يقدر أحد قدره

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p254#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p254#2/r1.speaker: عمرو بن أوس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p254#2/r1.claim: ʿAmr ibn Aws says that before Abraham's revelation, a person could be seized for another's sin; the principle then declared that no bearer bears another's burden.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p254#2/r1.anchor: عن عمرو بن أوس قال كان الرجل يؤخذ بذنب غيره عتى نزل

ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#5/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#5/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#5/r1.claim: Abraham’s reference is to what was in his revealed scrolls; he fulfilled what he was commanded or completely honored his covenant with God.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#5/r1.anchor: وبما في صحف إبراهيم التي نزلت عليه ( الذي وفى ( أي وفر وأتم ما أمر به

ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#5/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#5/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#5/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says Abraham fulfilled all ten ‘shares of Islam,’ which no one else did: ten in 9:111, ten in 33:35, six at the start of 23:1, and four in 70:26.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#5/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : وفى بسهام الإسلام كلها ولم يوفها

ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#5/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#5/r3.speaker: أبو أمامة
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#5/r3.claim: A weak raised report from Abu Umama says Abraham fulfilled four rakʿas that he prayed each day, in one version at the day’s beginning.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#5/r3.anchor: عن أبي أمامة يرفعه وفى بأربع ركعات يصليهن في كل يوم

ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#5/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#5/r4.speaker: معاذ بن أنس
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#5/r4.claim: A raised report from Muʿadh ibn Anas says God called Abraham His intimate because he fulfilled; he recited the morning-and-evening glorification in 30:17.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#5/r4.anchor: وأخرج أحمد من حديث معاذبن أنس مرفوعا أيضا ألا أخبركم

ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#5/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#5/r5.speaker: معاذ بن أنس
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#5/r5.claim: The report gives Abraham’s repeated morning and evening glorification as the practice in view.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#5/r5.anchor: كلما أصبح وأمسى سبحان الله حين تمسو وحين تصبحون الآية

ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#5/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#5/r6.speaker: عكرمة
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#5/r6.claim: Ikrima explains fulfillment as conveying the ten obligations beginning ‘no bearer bears another’s burden.’
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#5/r6.anchor: وقال عكرمة : ( وفي ) بتبليغ هذه العشرة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#5/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#5/r7.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#5/r7.claim: Al-Hasan reports the general interpretation, which al-Alusi prefers: Abraham fulfilled every command God gave him.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#5/r7.anchor: والأولى العموم وهو مروي عن الحسن

ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#5/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#5/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#5/r8.claim: Abraham was singled out for this quality because of what he endured; the sacrifice story alone suffices as evidence.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#5/r8.anchor: وتخصيصه عليه السلام بهذا الوصف لاحتمالأما لايحتمله

ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#5/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#5/r9.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#5/r9.claim: One explanation for naming these prophets is that earlier peoples assigned a person relatives’ sins; Abraham first opposed this, and Moses confirmed the rule.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#5/r9.anchor: قيل : لأنه فيما بين نوح وإبراهيم كانوا يأخذون الرجل

ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#5/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#5/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#5/r10.claim: Abraham is mentioned first because his scrolls were better known and more familiar to the audience.

ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#5/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#5/r11.speaker: أبو أمامة الباهلي وسعيد بن جبير وأبو مالك الغفاري وابن السمقيع وزيد بن علي
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#5/r11.claim: These readers pronounce the fāʾ lightly in وَفَى.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#5/r11.anchor: وقرأأبو أمامة الباهلي وسعيد بن جبير وأبو مالك الغفاري

DURR-FULL:v7p660/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p660/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p660/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says Abraham alone fulfilled all thirty portions of Islam: ten in 9:111, ten in 33:35, six beginning at 23:1, and four in 70:1, 70:26, and 70:27; fulfilling one portion counts as fulfilling that share.
DURR-FULL:v7p660/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {وإبراهيم الذي وفى} قال: وفى سهام الإسلام كلها ولم يوفها أحد غيره وهي ثلاثون سهما

DURR-FULL:v7p660/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p660/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p660/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says Abraham fulfilled the principle that no burdened soul bears another's burden, through the passage continuing to the ancient scrolls.
DURR-FULL:v7p660/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: لما نزلت {والنجم} فبلغ {وإبراهيم الذي وفى} قال: وفى {ألا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى} إلى قوله {من النذر الأولى}

DURR-FULL:v7p660/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p660/r3.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v7p660/r3.claim: Abu al-Aliya says Abraham carried out and conveyed the rule that no soul bears another's burden.
DURR-FULL:v7p660/r3.anchor: عن أبي العالية في قوله {وإبراهيم الذي وفى} قال: أدى عن ربه {ألا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى}

DURR-FULL:v7p660/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p660/r4.speaker: عمرو بن أوس
DURR-FULL:v7p660/r4.claim: Amr ibn Aws says people were once punished for another's sin until Abraham conveyed that no soul bears another's burden.
DURR-FULL:v7p660/r4.anchor: عن عمرو بن أوس قال: كان الرجل يؤخذ بذنب غيره حتى جاء إبراهيم فقال الله {وإبراهيم الذي وفى}

DURR-FULL:v7p660/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p660/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p660/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says that before Abraham people held a close relative responsible for another, until Abraham conveyed that no one is taken for another's sin.
DURR-FULL:v7p660/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس {وإبراهيم الذي وفى} قال: كانوا قبل إبراهيم يأخذون الولي بالمولى حتى كان إبراهيم فبلغ {ألا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى}

DURR-FULL:v7p660/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p660/r6.speaker: هذيل بن شرحبيل
DURR-FULL:v7p660/r6.claim: Hudhayl ibn Shurayhil says another's sin was borne from Noah to Abraham, who brought the rule that no soul bears another's burden.
DURR-FULL:v7p660/r6.anchor: عن هذيل بن شرحبيل قال: كان الرجل يؤخذ بذنب غيره فيما بين نوح إلى إبراهيم حتى جاء إبراهيم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r1.claim: The reference to Abraham includes the scrolls of Abraham.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r2.speaker: أبو ذر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r2.claim: Abu Dharr reports from the Prophet that God gave Abraham ten scrolls and Moses ten scrolls before the Torah.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r2.anchor: وفي حديث أبي ذر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن الله تعالى أنزل على إبراهيم عشر صحائف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وأبو عمران الجوني وابن السميفع اليماني
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r3.claim: These readers pronounce wafā with a light, undoubled fāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r3.anchor: قرأ سعيد بن جبير وأبو عمران الجوني وابن السميفع اليماني وفي بتخفيف الفاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r4.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the doubled form waffā is more emphatic than wafā because Abraham’s trial was among the greatest trials.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r4.anchor: قال الزجاج قوله وفى أبلغ من وفى لأن الذي امتحن به من أعظم المحن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r5.speaker: رسول الله
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r5.claim: A report from the Prophet says Abraham fulfilled his daily worship by performing four rakahs early in the day.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r5.anchor: رواه أبوأمامة عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r6.speaker: رسول الله
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r6.claim: A report says Abraham was called the faithful friend because he recited the evening and morning glorification in 30:17 each day.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r6.anchor: روى سهل بن معاذ بن أنس الجهني عن أبيه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r7.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس والقرظي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r7.claim: Al-Awfi’s report from Ibn Abbas, also held by al-Qurazi, says Abraham fulfilled his obedience in what he did concerning his son.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r7.anchor: أنه وفي الطاعة فيما فعل بابنه رواه العوفي عن ابن عباس وبه قال القرظي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r8.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r8.claim: Ikrima’s report from Ibn Abbas says Abraham fulfilled all the ordinances of Islam for his Lord.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r8.anchor: أنه وفى ربه جميع شرائع الإسلام روى هذا المعنى عكرمة عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r9.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says Abraham fulfilled what he was commanded to convey of the message.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r9.anchor: أنه وفى ما أمر به من تبليغ الرسالة روي عن ابن عباس أيضا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r10.speaker: الحسن وسعيد بن جبير وقتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r10.claim: Hasan, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, and Qatada say Abraham acted on what he was commanded.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r10.anchor: أنه عمل بما أمر به قاله الحسن وسعيد بن جبير وقتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r11.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r11.claim: Mujahid says Abraham fulfilled what was made obligatory upon him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r11.anchor: وقال مجاهد وفى ما فرض عليه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r12.speaker: عكرمة ومجاهد والنخعي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r12.claim: These authorities say Abraham fulfilled his task by conveying the verses beginning with the rule that no bearer bears another’s burden and those that follow.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r12.anchor: وهذا مروي عن عكرمة ومجاهد والنخعي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r13.speaker: الضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r13.claim: Al-Dahhak says Abraham fulfilled the rites of pilgrimage.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r14.speaker: عطاء بن السائب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r14.claim: Abraham vowed never to ask a created being for anything; when Gabriel asked whether he needed help in the fire, Abraham said no and kept his vow.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r14.anchor: فلما قذف في النار قال له جبريل ألك حاجة فقال أما إليك فلا فوفى بما عاهد ذكره عطاء بن السائب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r15.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r15.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r15.claim: Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna says Abraham fulfilled the trust.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#4/r15.anchor: أنه أدى الأمانة قاله سفيان بن عيينة

MUJAHID:v2p632/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p632/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUJAHID:v2p632/r1.claim: The Prophet says Abraham fulfilled his day's duty by performing four rakʿahs early in the day.
MUJAHID:v2p632/r1.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم هذه الآية ﴿ وإبراهيم الذي وفى ﴾ قال أتدرون ما وفى

MUJAHID:v2p632/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p632/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p632/r2.claim: Mujahid says Abraham fulfilled what had been prescribed for him.
MUJAHID:v2p632/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد قال يقول ﴿ وفي ﴾ ما فرض عليه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#6/r1.claim: Abraham is mentioned in the scrolls of Abraham; the following description concerns him.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#6/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#6/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#6/r2.claim: Waffā means he fulfilled or completed, as in the statement that God completed Abraham's tests; the wording broadly covers every kind of fulfillment.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#6/r2.anchor: اى وفر واتم كقوله فاتمهن واطلاقه ليتناول كل وفاء وتوفية

NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#6/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#6/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#6/r3.claim: A lightened form of the verb is also read; the doubled form emphasizes complete fulfillment.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#6/r3.anchor: وقرىء مخففا والتشديد مبالغة في الوفاء

NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#6/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#6/r4.speaker: الحسن
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#6/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan says Abraham fulfilled every command God gave him.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#6/r4.anchor: وعن الحسن ما أمره الله بشىء الا وفى به

NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#6/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#6/r5.speaker: عطاء بن السائب
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#6/r5.claim: ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib reports that Abraham pledged never to ask a created being for anything; when cast into the fire, he told Gabriel he had no need of him.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#6/r5.anchor: وعن عطاء بن السائب عهد ان لا يسأل مخلوقا فلما قذف في النار قال له جبريل

NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#6/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#6/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#6/r6.claim: The Prophet said Abraham fulfilled his daily practice with four rakʿas at the start of the day, the ḍuḥā prayer.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#6/r6.anchor: وعن النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم وفى عمله كل يوم باربع ركعات في صدر النهار وهى صلاة الضحى

NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#6/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#6/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#6/r7.claim: Another report says Abraham would recite the evening and morning glorification verses at those times; it explains why God called him the one who fulfilled.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#6/r7.anchor: وروى الا اخبركم لم سمى الله خليله الذى وفى كان يقول اذا اصبح واذا امسى

NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#6/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#6/r8.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#6/r8.claim: Another view says Abraham fulfilled the thirty portions of Islam: ten in al-Tawba, ten in al-Aḥzāb, and ten in al-Muʾminūn.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#6/r8.anchor: وقيل وفي سهام الاسلام وهى ثلاثون عشرة في التوبة التائبون وعشرة في الاحزاب

QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r9.claim: The unbeliever is asked whether he has heard what is in the scriptures of Moses and Abraham, who fulfilled what was required of him in himself, wealth, and child.
QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r9.anchor: أم لم ينبأ هذا الكافر بما في صحف موسى ، وصحف إبارهيم الذي وفى ؛ أي أتم ما طولب به في نفسه وماله وولده

TAB-FULL:v22p75/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p75/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p75/r1.claim: Al-Tabari explains Abraham's fulfillment as delivering to those he was sent to what he had been sent with.
TAB-FULL:v22p75/r1.anchor: وإبراهيم الذي وفى} [النجم: 37] يقول: وإبراهيم الذي وفى من أرسل إليه ما أرسل به.

TAB-FULL:v22p75/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p75/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v22p75/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says Abraham conveyed that no one is held accountable for another's sin, ending the earlier practice of taking one heir for another.
TAB-FULL:v22p75/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، {وإبراهيم الذي وفى} [النجم: 37] قال: «كانوا قبل إبراهيم يأخذون الولي بالولي، حتى كان إبراهيم، فبلغ»

TAB-FULL:v22p75/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p75/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v22p75/r3.claim: Mujahid, through Ikrima, says Abraham fulfilled his mission by conveying the verses beginning with the rule that no bearer bears another's burden.
TAB-FULL:v22p75/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد، عن عكرمة، {وإبراهيم الذي وفى} [النجم: 37] قالوا: «بلغ هذه الآيات»

TAB-FULL:v22p75/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p75/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v22p75/r4.claim: Qatada says Abraham fulfilled obedience to God and delivered his Lord's messages to creation.
TAB-FULL:v22p75/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله {وإبراهيم الذي وفى} [النجم: 37] قال: «وفى طاعة الله، وبلغ رسالات ربه إلى خلقه»

TAB-FULL:v22p75/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p75/r5.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v22p75/r5.claim: Ikrima says Abraham fulfilled the ten verses from the statement that no bearer bears another's burden through the statement about the second creation.
TAB-FULL:v22p75/r5.anchor: وكان عكرمة يقول: وفى هؤلاء الآيات العشر {ألا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى} [النجم: 38] حتى بلغ {وأن عليه النشأة الأخرى} [النجم: 47]

TAB-FULL:v22p75/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p75/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v22p75/r6.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says Abraham delivered what he was commanded to deliver.
TAB-FULL:v22p75/r6.anchor: عن أبي حصين، عن سعيد بن جبير، في قوله:

TAB-FULL:v22p75/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p75/r7.speaker: سفيان
TAB-FULL:v22p75/r7.claim: Sufyan glosses Abraham's fulfillment as having delivered the message.

TAB-FULL:v22p75/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p75/r8.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v22p75/r8.claim: Ibn Zayd says Abraham fulfilled the messages of his Lord by delivering what he had been sent with, as a messenger should.
TAB-FULL:v22p75/r8.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {وإبراهيم الذي وفى} [النجم: 37] قال: " وفى: بلغ رسالات ربه، بلغ ما أرسل به

TAB-FULL:v22p75/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p75/r9.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v22p75/r9.claim: Another view says Abraham fulfilled his dream of sacrificing his son and reads the burden verse as fronted in meaning, linking it to what is in Moses' and Abraham's scrolls.
TAB-FULL:v22p75/r9.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل وفى بما رأى في المنام من ذبح ابنه، وقالوا قوله: {ألا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى} [النجم: 38]

SULAMI:v2p287#5/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p287#5/r1.speaker: anonymous
SULAMI:v2p287#5/r1.claim: An unnamed saying describes Abraham as leaving self behind in bearing trials and witnessing every trial as a blessing in God's presence.
SULAMI:v2p287#5/r1.anchor: قال : خرج من نفسه فيما تحمل خفض محنه فشاهد المحن كلها نعمة في جنبه ومشاهدته .

SULAMI:v2p287#5/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p287#5/r2.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p287#5/r2.claim: Ibn Ata says Abraham fulfilled four offerings: himself for the fire, his heart for the Merciful, his son for sacrifice, and his wealth for his brothers.
SULAMI:v2p287#5/r2.anchor: قال ابن عطاء رحمة الله عليه : وفى بأربعة أشياء نفسه للنيران وقلبه للرحمن وولده للقربان

SULAMI:v2p287#5/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p287#5/r3.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v2p287#5/r3.claim: Ja'far defines fulfillment as witnessing sincerity and faithfulness in every condition and deed.
SULAMI:v2p287#5/r3.anchor: قال جعفر : معاينة الصدق والوفاء في كل حال وفعل .

SULAMI:v2p287#5/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p287#5/r4.speaker: أبو القاسم
SULAMI:v2p287#5/r4.claim: Abu al-Qasim says Abraham surrendered wealth, son, and spirit to God: he preserved himself in the fire and laid his son down for sacrifice, which God ransomed.
SULAMI:v2p287#5/r4.anchor: سمعت أبا القاسم قال : وفى بتسليم المال والولد والروح لله في الدنيا في نفسه بحفظها حين ألقى في النار

FARRA:v3p100/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p100/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p100/r6.claim: Abraham fulfilled the teaching that no burdened soul bears another’s burden.
FARRA:v3p100/r6.anchor: «وإبراهيم الذي وفى» (37) : بلغ- أن ليست تزر وازرة وزر أخرى، لا تحتمل الوازرة ذنب غيرها.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p65#3/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p65#3/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p65#3/r1.claim: The reference is to what was in Abraham's scriptures.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p65#3/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p65#3/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p65#3/r2.claim: Tawfiyah means completion and fulfillment; the author illustrates it with God fully paying people's wages.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p65#3/r2.anchor: معنى التوفية في اللغة الإتمام والإكمال، يقال: وفيته أجره

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p65#3/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p65#3/r3.speaker: ابن عباس في رواية عطاء والكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p65#3/r3.claim: One view says Abraham fulfilled by delivering to his people what God had commanded him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p65#3/r3.anchor: فقال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء والكلبي: بلغ ما أمر به قومه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p65#3/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p65#3/r4.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p65#3/r4.claim: Muqatil gives the same interpretation: Abraham delivered God's command to his people.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p65#3/r4.anchor: بلغ ما أمر به قومه، وهو قول مقاتل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p65#3/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p65#3/r5.speaker: الفراء وابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p65#3/r5.claim: Al-Farraʾ and Ibn Qutayba choose the interpretation that Abraham delivered God's command to his people.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p65#3/r5.anchor: بلغ ما أمر به قومه، وهو قول مقاتل، واختيار الفراء، وابن قتيبة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p65#3/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p65#3/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير، وإبراهيم، ومجاهد، وأبو العالية، وعكرمة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p65#3/r6.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Ibrahim, Mujahid, Abu al-Aliya, and Ikrima also say Abraham conveyed the words from God to his people.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p65#3/r6.anchor: وهو قول سعيد بن جبير، وإبراهيم، ومجاهد، وأبي العالية، وعكرمة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p66/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p66/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p66/r1.claim: Under the first interpretation, the particle an in the following verse is accusative as governed by waffā.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p66/r1.anchor: وأن على هذا القول في محل النصب بقوله: (وفي)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p66/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p66/r2.speaker: جماعة من المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p66/r2.claim: Another view says Abraham fulfilled every duty God imposed, including sacrificing his son, enduring the fire, passing the tests of 2:124, circumcision, and pilgrimage rites.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p66/r2.anchor: وقال آخرون: معنى: (وفي) أكمل ما يجب لله تعالى عليه بالطاعة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p66/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p66/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p66/r3.claim: Abu Ishaq prefers the view that Abraham completed all obligations through obedience and patience.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p66/r3.anchor: وهو اختيار أبي إسحاق، وعلى هذا موضع أن في قوله

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p429#5/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p429#5/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p429#5/r1.claim: Waffā means that Abraham reached or accomplished the intended end.

ITQAN:v4p530/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p530/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v4p530/r1.claim: In a weak-chain report from Abu Umama, the Prophet says Abraham fulfilled his day's worship with four units of prayer early in the morning.
ITQAN:v4p530/r1.anchor: أخرج ابن جرير وابن أبي حاتم بسند ضعيف عن أبي أمامة قال تلا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم هذه الآية ﴿ وإبراهيم الذي وفى ﴾

ITQAN:v4p530/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p530/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v4p530/r2.claim: A report from Muadh ibn Anas says God named Abraham His intimate friend because he recited the evening and morning glorification every morning and evening.
ITQAN:v4p530/r2.anchor: عن معاذ بن أنس عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال ألا أخبركم لم سمي الله إبراهيم خليله

RAZI-FULL:v29p11#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p11#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p11#2/r1.claim: The scrolls passage and the statement that one burdened soul bears no other's burden correspond to 53:30–31, since both passages explain recompense.

RAZI-FULL:v29p11#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p11#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p11#2/r2.claim: Rāzī proposes a shift from idolaters to scriptured people: a person with a book gave God's rights for a short time, then stopped when Muhammad came; the scrolls already taught individual accountability, so the man may be from the People of the Book.
RAZI-FULL:v29p11#2/r2.anchor: يمكن أن يقال : إن الله تعالى لما بين حال المشركين

RAZI-FULL:v29p13/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p13/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p13/r4.claim: The apparent sense of وفّى is fulfilling covenants, with the doubled form intensifying the sense; Abraham fulfilled his vow and submitted his son to sacrifice, as the dream was confirmed.
RAZI-FULL:v29p13/r4.anchor: أنه الوفاء الذي يذكر في العهود وعلى هذا فالتشديد للمبالغة

RAZI-FULL:v29p13/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p13/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p13/r5.claim: Another reading derives وفّى from completing: Abraham completed God's trials, as in the verse saying he completed the words with which his Lord tested him.
RAZI-FULL:v29p13/r5.anchor: أنه من التوفية التي من الوفاء وهو التمام والتوفية الإتمام

RAZI-FULL:v29p13/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p13/r6.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v29p13/r6.claim: A further interpretation says Abraham rendered God's bodily rights, directly contrasting him with the person who gave little and stopped.
RAZI-FULL:v29p13/r6.anchor: أي أعطى حقوق الله في بدنه

RAZI-FULL:v29p13/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p13/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p13/r7.claim: Rāzī explains Abraham's fulfillment by saying he kept his promise to seek forgiveness for his father and did so; God's refusal taught that each person receives only the fruits of his own effort and no soul bears another's sin.
RAZI-FULL:v29p13/r7.anchor: فاستغفر ووفى بالعهد ولم يغفر الله له

RAZI-FULL:v29p13/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p13/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p13/r8.claim: Abraham was praised as وفّى because Jews, polytheists, and Muslims all accepted this description, whereas polytheists might hesitate to praise Moses.
RAZI-FULL:v29p13/r8.anchor: فلأنه كان متفقا عليه بين اليهود والمشركين والمسلمين

STUDYQURAN:53:36/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:36/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:36/r2.claim: Abraham fulfilled by enduring trials none else endured, including being cast into the fire for breaking idols and agreeing to sacrifice his son before Gabriel stopped him.
STUDYQURAN:53:36/r2.anchor: Abraham is referred to as he who fulfilled for patiently enduring what no one else was made to endure

STUDYQURAN:53:36/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:36/r3.speaker: IK, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:53:36/r3.claim: Another view is that Abraham fulfilled the command to deliver God’s message.
STUDYQURAN:53:36/r3.anchor: Others say this verse refers to Abraham’s fulfillment of the command to deliver God’s message (IK, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:53:36/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:36/r4.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:53:36/r4.claim: A further view is that Abraham fulfilled his covenant with God.
STUDYQURAN:53:36/r4.anchor: or to Abraham fulfilling the covenant with God (R)

TAB-FULL:v22p77/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p77/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
TAB-FULL:v22p77/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says Abraham completed obedience through what he did with his son after the dream; the scrolls of Moses state that no bearer bears another's burden, through the rest of the verse.
TAB-FULL:v22p77/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {أم لم ينبأ بما في صحف موسى

TAB-FULL:v22p77/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p77/r2.speaker: القرظي
TAB-FULL:v22p77/r2.claim: Al-Qurazi says Abraham fulfilled his duty by being ready to sacrifice his son.
TAB-FULL:v22p77/r2.anchor: عن القرظي، وسئل، عن هذه الآية

TAB-FULL:v22p77/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p77/r3.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v22p77/r3.claim: Another reported view is that Abraham fulfilled all the ordinances of Islam.
TAB-FULL:v22p77/r3.anchor: وقال آخرون بل معنى ذلك: أنه وفى ربه جميع شرائع الإسلام

TAB-FULL:v22p77/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p77/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v22p77/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says Islam has thirty portions, no one tested by this religion established it as Abraham did, and God granted him exemption from the Fire.
TAB-FULL:v22p77/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: «الإسلام ثلاثون سهما

TAB-FULL:v22p77/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p77/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v22p77/r5.claim: Mujahid says Abraham fulfilled what was prescribed for him.

TAB-FULL:v22p77/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p77/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v22p77/r6.claim: A report says God named Abraham His intimate friend because morning and evening he recited the verse beginning فسبحان الله حين تمسون وحين تصبحون, through its end.
TAB-FULL:v22p77/r6.anchor: عن سهل بن معاذ بن أنس

TAB-FULL:v22p77/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p77/r7.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v22p77/r7.claim: Another view says Abraham fulfilled his Lord's work for the day; a report from Abu Umama has the Prophet explain that he performed four daytime rakahs.
TAB-FULL:v22p77/r7.anchor: ذكر من قال ذلك: حدثنا أبو كريب قال: ثنا الحسن بن عطية قال: ثنا إسرائيل، عن جعفر بن الزبير، عن القاسم، عن أبي أمامة

TAB-FULL:v22p77/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p77/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p77/r8.claim: Tabari prefers that Abraham fulfilled all the ordinances of Islam and every commanded act of obedience, because the report about his fulfillment is general and does not single out one act.
TAB-FULL:v22p77/r8.anchor: وأولى الأقوال في ذلك بالصواب قول من قال: وفى جميع شرائع الإسلام وجميع ما أمر به من الطاعة

TAB-FULL:v22p77/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p77/r9.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p77/r9.claim: The statement that no bearer bears another's burden is cited as material in the scrolls of Moses and Abraham, not as a restriction defining what Abraham fulfilled.
TAB-FULL:v22p77/r9.anchor: فإن ذلك مما أخبر الله جل ثناؤه أنه في صحف موسى وإبراهيم، لا مما خص به الخبر

TAB-FULL:v22p77/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p77/r10.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p77/r10.claim: Tabari says he would follow either prophetic report if sound, but their chains raise concerns that require verification.
TAB-FULL:v22p77/r10.anchor: ولكن في إسنادهما نظر يجب التثبت فيهما من أجله

BURSEVI:v9p201/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p201/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p201/r6.claim: Abraham is coordinated with Moses: the phrase means what was in Abraham's scrolls; he fulfilled what he was tested with or commanded without omission.
BURSEVI:v9p201/r6.anchor: عطف على موسى أي وبما في صحف ابراهيم الذي وفي أي وفر وأتم ما ابتلي به من الكلمات

BURSEVI:v9p201/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p201/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p201/r7.claim: Waffā means to give fully; its intensified form can stress Abraham's exceptional fulfillment of his covenant with God.
BURSEVI:v9p201/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون التشديد فيه للتكثير والمبالغة في الوفاء بما عاهد الله

BURSEVI:v9p201/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p201/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p201/r8.claim: Abraham merited the description through extraordinary trials: Nimrod's fire, offering his son, migration, leaving family in a barren valley, and seeking guests or fasting when none came.
BURSEVI:v9p201/r8.anchor: وتخصيصه بذلك لاحتماله ما لم يحتمل غيره بالصبر على نار نمرود حتى أنه أتاه جبريل حين ألقى في النار

BURSEVI:v9p201/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p201/r9.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v9p201/r9.claim: A report from the Prophet links Abraham's daily fulfillment to four rakʿahs, the Duha prayer; a sacred hadith promises sufficiency for the day to one praying four early rakʿahs.
BURSEVI:v9p201/r9.anchor: وعن النبي عليه السلام وفي عمل كل يوم بأربع ركعات وهي صلاة الضحى

BURSEVI:v9p201/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p201/r10.speaker: الحديث القدسي
BURSEVI:v9p201/r10.claim: A sacred hadith quotes God telling Adam's child to pray four rakʿahs early in the day, promising sufficiency for its remainder.
BURSEVI:v9p201/r10.anchor: وفي الحديث القدسي : (ابن آدم أركع إلى أربع ركعات من أرول النهار أكفك آخره)

BURSEVI:v9p201/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p201/r11.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v9p201/r11.claim: The Prophet reportedly said Abraham was called faithful because he recited the evening and morning glorifications through the end of the two verses.
BURSEVI:v9p201/r11.anchor: وروى إلا أخبركم لم سمى الله خليله الذي وفى كان يقول : إذا أصبح وأمسى فسبحان الله

BURSEVI:v9p201/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p201/r12.speaker: أبو ذر الغفاري
BURSEVI:v9p201/r12.claim: Abū Dharr reports 104 revealed books: ten pages to Adam, fifty to Seth, thirty to Idrīs, ten to Abraham, and the Torah, Gospel, Psalms, and Quran.
BURSEVI:v9p201/r12.anchor: وعن أبي ذر الغفاري رضي الله عنه قال : قلت : يا رسول الله كم من كتاب أنمل الله؟

BURSEVI:v9p201/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p201/r13.speaker: صحف إبراهيم
BURSEVI:v9p201/r13.claim: Abraham's scrolls counsel a king not to amass worldly wealth but to answer the oppressed person's prayer, even if the oppressed is an unbeliever.
BURSEVI:v9p201/r13.anchor: أيها الملك المبتلي المغرور إني لم أبعثك فتجمع الدنيا بعضها إلى بعض

BURSEVI:v9p201/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p201/r14.speaker: صحف إبراهيم
BURSEVI:v9p201/r14.claim: The scrolls say a wise person should reserve time for prayer, reflection, self-accounting, and lawful needs, stay aware of his era, and guard his tongue because speech is among one's deeds.
BURSEVI:v9p201/r14.anchor: وعلى العاقل ما لم يكن مغلوبا على عقله أن يكون له ساعات ساعة يناجي فيها ربه

BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r1.claim: Moses precedes Abraham by progression from the nearer and better-known figure; Moses truly had a revealed book, unlike Abraham.
BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r1.anchor: هو من باب الترقي من الأقرب إلى الأبعد لكون الأقرب أعرف وأيضا أن موسى صاحب كتاب حقيقة بخلاف إبراهيم

TABATABAI:53:33-37/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r2.claim: The story and citations from Moses’ and Abraham’s scriptures clarify the truth against the polytheists’ claim that idols represented God’s daughters, the angels, whom they worshiped for intercession; earlier verses refuted that claim.
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r2.anchor: أشار سبحانه بالتعرض لهذه القصة ونقل ما من صحف إبراهيم وموسى عليهما السلام إلى بيان وجه الحق فيها

TABATABAI:53:33-37/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r3.claim: The passage establishes that creation and governance belong to God and lead to a second life of recompense, which entails revealed religion and duties; the destruction of Noah’s, ‘Ad’s, Thamud’s, and the overturned cities’ peoples is evidence.
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r3.anchor: وهو أن الخلق والتدبير لله سبحانه، إليه ينتهي كل ذلك

TABATABAI:53:33-37/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r4.claim: After these scriptural teachings, the surah warns that this warner belongs to the earlier warners, says the Hour is near, and ends by commanding prostration and worship.
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r4.anchor: ثم عقب سبحانه هذا الذي نقله عن صحف النبيين الكريمين بالتنبيه على أن هذا النذير من النذر الأولى الخالية

TABATABAI:53:33-37/r15.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r15.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r15.claim: Abraham’s fulfillment means that he fully and perfectly discharged his duty of servitude.
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r15.anchor: وتوفيته عليه السلام تأديته ما عليه من الحق في العبودية أتم التأدية وأبلغها

TABATABAI:53:38-39/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:38-39/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:38-39/r1.claim: The phrase about Abraham fulfilling his duty is illustrated by the verse saying he completed the trials imposed by his Lord.
TABATABAI:53:38-39/r1.anchor: وإذ ابتلى إبراهيم ربه بكلمات فأتمهن

TABRISI:53:32-39/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:32-39/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:53:32-39/r13.claim: The reference is to the books of the Torah and the pages of Abraham; waffā means Abraham completed and fulfilled what he was commanded.
TABRISI:53:32-39/r13.anchor: أي بل ألم يخبر ولم يحدث بما في أسفار التوراة

TABRISI:53:32-39/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:32-39/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:53:32-39/r14.claim: Other explanations say Abraham conveyed the message to his people, or completed everything God required and tested him with.
TABRISI:53:32-39/r14.anchor: وقيل: بلغ قومه وأدى ما أمر به إليهم

THALABI:v9p151/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p151/r9.speaker: عكرمة وطاوس عن ابن عباس
THALABI:v9p151/r9.claim: Ikrima and Tawus transmit from Ibn Abbas that before Abraham people punished relatives for another person’s crime, even executing kin, spouses, or masters for others; Abraham forbade this and conveyed that no bearer bears another’s burden.
THALABI:v9p151/r9.anchor: روى عكرمة وطاوس عن ابن عباس قال: كانوا قبل إبراهيم صلوات الله عليه يأخذون الرجل بذنب غيره

THALABI:v9p151/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p151/r10.speaker: الحسن وسعيد بن جبير وقتادة وابن زيد
THALABI:v9p151/r10.claim: These authorities say Abraham fulfilled what he was commanded and delivered his Lord’s messages to creation.
THALABI:v9p151/r10.anchor: وقال الحسن وسعيد بن جبير وقتادة وابن زيد: عمل بما أمر به وبلغ رسالات ربه الى خلقه

THALABI:v9p151/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p151/r11.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v9p151/r11.claim: Mujahid says Abraham fulfilled what was prescribed for him.

THALABI:v9p151/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p151/r12.speaker: ربيع
THALABI:v9p151/r12.claim: Rabi says Abraham fulfilled his vision by undertaking the sacrifice of his son.
THALABI:v9p151/r12.anchor: ربيع: وفى رؤياه وقام بذبح ابنه

THALABI:v9p151/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p151/r13.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
THALABI:v9p151/r13.claim: Ata al-Khurasani says Abraham fulfilled obedience.

THALABI:v9p151/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p151/r14.speaker: أبو العالية
THALABI:v9p151/r14.claim: Abu al-Aliya says Abraham completed Islam, fulfilling all its obligations, as in 2:124; he says no one else fully established every part of this religion.
THALABI:v9p151/r14.anchor: أبو العالية: وفى بتمام الإسلام وهو قوله: وإذ ابتلى إبراهيم ربه بكلمات فأتمهن

THALABI:v9p151/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p151/r15.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p151/r15.claim: Tawfiya means completion, as in fulfilling and fully paying a right; the author cites the Qur’anic phrase ‘to pay them their rewards.’
THALABI:v9p151/r15.anchor: والتوفية: الإتمام. فقال: وفيت عليه حقه ووفرته، قال الله سبحانه: ليوفيهم أجورهم

THALABI:v9p151/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p151/r16.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
THALABI:v9p151/r16.claim: Sufyan ibn Uyayna says Abraham fulfilled the trust.

THALABI:v9p152/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p152/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p152/r1.claim: Abraham fulfilled his obligation concerning the rites.
THALABI:v9p152/r1.anchor: وفى بشأن المناسك. عطاء بن السائب

THALABI:v9p152/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p152/r2.speaker: عطاء بن السائب
THALABI:v9p152/r2.claim: Aṭā reports that Abraham vowed never to ask a creature for anything; when Gabriel asked whether he needed anything in the fire, Abraham said no, and God praised his fidelity.
THALABI:v9p152/r2.anchor: عطاء بن السائب: بلغني أن إبراهيم كان عهد أن لا يسأل مخلوقا شيئا

THALABI:v9p152/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p152/r3.speaker: الحسين ابن الفضل
THALABI:v9p152/r3.claim: Al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl says Abraham fulfilled his duty to guests, earning the name Father of Guests.
THALABI:v9p152/r3.anchor: الحسين ابن الفضل: وفى بشأن الأضياف حتى سمي أبا الأضياف

THALABI:v9p152/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p152/r4.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
THALABI:v9p152/r4.claim: Al-Warrāq says Abraham fulfilled the condition of his claim: after declaring submission when God commanded it, he proved his claim through trials of wealth, child, and self.
THALABI:v9p152/r4.anchor: أبو بكر الوراق: قام بشرط ما ادعى، وذلك ان الله سبحانه قال له: أسلم قال: أسلمت

THALABI:v9p152/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p152/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v9p152/r5.claim: A report from the Prophet explains Abraham's fulfillment as regularly reciting the verse beginning Subḥāna Allāh ḥīna tumsūna waḥīna tuṣbiḥū in the morning and evening, through its end.
THALABI:v9p152/r5.anchor: عن سهل عن أبيه عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: «ألا أخبركم لم سمى تعالى إبراهيم خليله الذي وفى

THALABI:v9p152#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p152#2/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v9p152#2/r1.claim: In a report from Abū Umāma, the Prophet explains Abraham's fulfillment as performing four rakʿas at the start of the day.
THALABI:v9p152#2/r1.anchor: قالوا: الله ورسوله أعلم، قال: وفى: يعني عمل يومه بأربع ركعات كان يصليهن من أول النهار

THALABI:v9p152#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p152#2/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v9p152#2/r2.claim: A divine saying transmitted from the Prophet tells the son of Adam not to neglect four early-morning rakʿas, promising sufficiency for the rest of the day.
THALABI:v9p152#2/r2.anchor: عن نعيم بن همار أنه سمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: «قال الله تعالى: يا بن آدم لا تعجز عن أربع ركعات

THALABI:v9p152#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p152#2/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
THALABI:v9p152#2/r3.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr read وفّى without doubling the fāʾ.
THALABI:v9p152#2/r3.anchor: عن أبي يزيد عن سعيد بن جبير أنه قرأ وإبراهيم الذي وفى خفيفة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:36-44/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:36-44/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:36-44/r2.claim: Abraham fulfilled completely everything he had been commanded to do.

QASHANI:53:37-39/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:53:37-39/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:53:37-39/r1.claim: Abraham fulfilled God's due by surrendering existence in annihilating unity, serving and conveying the message in steadfast subsistence, or by completing the words and qualities God tested him with.
QASHANI:53:37-39/r1.anchor: حق الله عليه بتسليم الوجود إليه حال الفناء في التوحيد

QASHANI:53:37-39/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:53:37-39/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:53:37-39/r2.claim: A lightened reading of waffā means Abraham kept his primordial covenant, remaining faithful until he attained unity.
QASHANI:53:37-39/r2.anchor: وقرىء: { وفى } ، مخففا، أي: بعهده المأخوذ ميثاقه عليه

ELMALILI:53:33-54/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:33-54/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:33-54/r5.claim: Abraham fulfilled all the words with which he was commanded and tried, remaining faithful to his commitments in every matter; 2:124 is cited.
ELMALILI:53:33-54/r5.anchor: mantûkunca me’mur ve mübtelâ olduğu kelimâtı tamamıyla îfâ etmişti.

ELMALILI:53:33-54/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:33-54/r6.speaker: Ebû Hayyân
ELMALILI:53:33-54/r6.claim: Abu Hayyan reports a view that before Abraham people were held liable for relatives' or masters' crimes; Abraham first rejected this, and from his law to Moses's law people were not charged with another's crime.
ELMALILI:53:33-54/r6.anchor: Ebû Hayyân Bahr’da şöyle der: “Mûsâ ile İbrâhim, bu iki peygamberin tahsîsi için denilmiştir ki: Nûh ile İbrâhim

DAMGHANI:v1p490/r13.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p490/r13.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p490/r13.claim: Waffā means he completed or fulfilled; Abraham fully carried out what was required of him.

NAHHAS:v4p276/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p276/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v4p276/r2.claim: Ikrima transmits from Ibn ʿAbbas that the teaching about Abraham's fulfillment preceded Abraham.
NAHHAS:v4p276/r2.anchor: وروى عكرمة عن ابن عباس ( وإبراهيم الذي وفى ) قال كان قبل إبراهيم

NAHHAS:v4p276/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p276/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p276/r3.claim: The clause about Abraham is taken in the nominative position as an explanation of the principle that no bearer bears another's burden.
NAHHAS:v4p276/r3.anchor: فيؤخذ موضع رفع أي ذلك ألا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى

NAHHAS:v4p276/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p276/r4.speaker: مجاهد
NAHHAS:v4p276/r4.claim: Mujahid says Abraham fulfilled what had been imposed on him.
NAHHAS:v4p276/r4.anchor: والتقدير عند مجاهد وفى بما افترض عليه

NAHHAS:v4p276/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p276/r5.speaker: محمد بن كعب
NAHHAS:v4p276/r5.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb says Abraham fulfilled his duty by sacrificing his son.
NAHHAS:v4p276/r5.anchor: قال محمد بن كعب وفى بذبح ابنه

NAHHAS:v4p276/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p276/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p276/r6.claim: Al-Nahhas prefers the general sense that Abraham fulfilled every obligation of the Islamic law; the Arabic verb conveys abundant or complete fulfillment.
NAHHAS:v4p276/r6.anchor: وأولى ما قيل في معنى الآية بالصواب ما دل عليه عمومها أي وفى بكل ما افترض عليه بشرائع الإسلام ووفى في العربية للتكثير

ZAJJAJ:v5p75/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p75/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p75/r1.claim: Abraham fulfilled what he was commanded and tested with, including resolving to sacrifice his son, enduring his people's hostility and the fire, and circumcision.
ZAJJAJ:v5p75/r1.anchor: يقال إن إبراهيم - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وفى ما أمر به، وما امتحن به من ذبح ولده، فعزم على ذلك حتى فداه الله بالذبح

ZAJJAJ:v5p75/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p75/r2.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v5p75/r2.claim: A strengthened form of the verb waffā is said to be more emphatic than wafā because Abraham's trials were exceptionally severe.
ZAJJAJ:v5p75/r2.anchor: وقيل وفى وهي أبلغ من وفى لأن الذي امتحن به من أعظم المحن

ZAJJAJ:v5p75/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p75/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p75/r3.claim: The question asks whether he was informed of what was in Moses' and Abraham's scrolls; the text then states the scrolls' contents.
ZAJJAJ:v5p75/r3.anchor: أي أم لم يخبر، ثم أعلم ما في الصحف

ASAD-NOTES:53:33#n30/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:53:33#n30/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:53:33#n30/r1.claim: Asad cross-references 2:124 and says Moses and Abraham exemplify how prophets throughout history conveyed enduring ethical truths.
ASAD-NOTES:53:33#n30/r1.anchor: Cf. 2:124 and the corresponding note 100. It is obvious that the names of Abraham and Moses are cited here only by way of example

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p254/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p254/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p254/r2.claim: Qatāda says Abraham fulfilled obedience to God and his message to creation.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p254/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ الذي وفى ﴾ قال أوفى طاعة الله ورسالته إلى خلقه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414#2/r3.claim: The reference is to what is written in the scrolls of Abraham.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414#2/r4.claim: Waffa means Abraham completed what he had been commanded.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414#2/r5.speaker: الحسن وسعيد بن جبير وقتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414#2/r5.claim: Al-Hasan, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, and Qatada say Abraham did what he was commanded and delivered his Lord's messages to creation.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414#2/r5.anchor: قال الحسن، وسعيد بن جبير، وقتادة: عمل بما أمر به وبلغ رسالات ربه إلى خلقه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414#2/r6.claim: Mujahid says Abraham fulfilled what had been imposed on him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414#2/r6.anchor: قال مجاهد: وفى بما فرض عليه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414#2/r7.speaker: الربيع
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414#2/r7.claim: Al-Rabi says Abraham fulfilled his vision and carried out the sacrifice of his son.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414#2/r7.anchor: قال الربيع: وفى رؤياه وقام بذبح ابنه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414#2/r8.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414#2/r8.claim: Ata al-Khurasani says Abraham completed obedience.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414#2/r9.speaker: أبو العالية
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414#2/r9.claim: Abu al-Aliyya says Abraham fulfilled Islam's obligations, citing God's test with words and Abraham completing them; tawfiyah means completion.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414#2/r9.anchor: وقال أبو العالية: وفى سهام الإسلام. وهو قوله: "وإذ ابتلى إبراهيم ربه بكلمات فأتمهن"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414#2/r10.speaker: الضحاك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414#2/r10.claim: Al-Dahhak says Abraham fulfilled the covenant of the rites.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414#2/r11.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414#2/r11.claim: A report from the Prophet explains Abraham's fulfillment as praying four rakahs early in the day.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414#2/r11.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "إبراهيم الذي وفى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414#2/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414#2/r12.speaker: الله تعالى
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414#2/r12.claim: In a divine report through Abu al-Darda and Abu Dharr, God tells Adam's child to pray four rakahs early in the day and promises to suffice him for the rest of it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414#2/r12.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الله تبارك وتعالى أنه قال: "ابن آدم اركع لي أربع ركعات من أول النهار أكفك آخره"

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:36-38/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:36-38/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:36-38/r1.claim: Ibrāhīm fulfilled and completed what he undertook and was commanded to do; alternatively, he fully kept his covenant with God.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:36-38/r1.anchor: وفى وأتم ما التزمه وأمر به

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:36-38/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:36-38/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:36-38/r2.claim: The alternative is that he went to great lengths to fulfill his covenant with God.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:36-38/r2.anchor: أو بالغ في الوفاء بما عاهد الله

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:36-38/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:36-38/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:36-38/r3.claim: His fidelity is illustrated by enduring Nimrod's fire, declining Gabriel's offer of help, preparing to sacrifice his son, and seeking a guest daily, fasting if he found none.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:36-38/r3.anchor: كالصبر على نار نمروذ حتى أتاه جبريل

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:36-38/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:36-38/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:36-38/r4.claim: Among the examples are sacrificing his son and walking a parasang daily to seek a guest, intending to fast if none appeared.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:36-38/r4.anchor: وذبح الولد وأنه كان يمشي كل يوم فرسخا يرتاد ضيفا

BIQAI-FULL:v7p329/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p329/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p329/r8.claim: Abraham fully fulfilled commands and trials: he was the first to emigrate, endured the test of sacrificing his son and the fire, and sought no creature’s help.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p329/r8.anchor: ومدحه بقوله دالا بتشديد الفعل على غاية الوفاء : { الذي وفى } أي أتم ما أمر به وما امتحن به وما قلق شيئا من قلق

DURR-FULL:v7p658/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p658/r4.speaker: دراج أبو السمح
DURR-FULL:v7p658/r4.claim: Darraj says the passage was revealed after a man who could not get a mount from the Prophet was offered transport by another man so he could catch the army.
DURR-FULL:v7p658/r4.anchor: عن دراج أبي السمح قال: خرجت سرية غازية فسأل رجل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يحمله فقال: لا أجد ما أحملك عليه

DURR-FULL:v7p659/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p659/r5.speaker: أبو أمامة
DURR-FULL:v7p659/r5.claim: A weakly graded report says Abraham fulfilled his day's work through four early-day prayers, identified as the Duha prayer.
DURR-FULL:v7p659/r5.anchor: عن أبي أمامة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: أتدرون ما قوله {وإبراهيم الذي وفى} قالوا: الله ورسوله أعلم

DURR-FULL:v7p659/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p659/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p659/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says Abraham fulfilled God's command by conveying the message.
DURR-FULL:v7p659/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {وإبراهيم الذي وفى} قال: وفى الله بالبلاغ

DURR-FULL:v7p659/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p659/r7.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p659/r7.claim: Mujahid says Abraham fulfilled what God made obligatory upon him.
DURR-FULL:v7p659/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {وإبراهيم الذي وفى} قال: وفى ما فرض عليه

DURR-FULL:v7p659/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p659/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p659/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says Islam has thirty shares, none practiced before Abraham, and cites the verse as evidence.
DURR-FULL:v7p659/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: سهام الإسلام ثلاثون سهما لم يمسها أحد قبل إبراهيم عليه الصلاة والسلام قال الله {وإبراهيم الذي وفى}

DURR-FULL:v7p659/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p659/r9.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p659/r9.claim: Qatada says Abraham fulfilled obedience to God and conveyed his Lord's message to creation.
DURR-FULL:v7p659/r9.anchor: عن قتادة {وإبراهيم الذي وفى} قال: وفى طاعة الله وبلغ رسالة ربه إلى خلقه

DURR-FULL:v7p659/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p659/r10.speaker: مجاهد وعكرمة
DURR-FULL:v7p659/r10.claim: Mujahid and Ikrima say Abraham fulfilled the command to convey the statement that no bearer bears another's burden.
DURR-FULL:v7p659/r10.anchor: عن مجاهد وعكرمة {وإبراهيم الذي وفى} قال: بلغ هذه الآية {ألا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى}

DURR-FULL:v7p659/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p659/r11.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v7p659/r11.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says Abraham conveyed what he had been commanded.
DURR-FULL:v7p659/r11.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير {وإبراهيم الذي وفى} قال: بلغ ما أمر به

DURR-FULL:v7p659/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p659/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p659/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas says Abraham completed obedience in what he did with his son after the dream, and fulfilled the statement in Moses's scrolls that no bearer bears another's burden.
DURR-FULL:v7p659/r12.anchor: عن ابن عباس {وإبراهيم الذي وفى} يقول: الذي استكمل الطاعة فيما فعل بابنه حين رأى الرؤيا والذي في صحف موسى {ألا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى}

DURR-FULL:v7p659/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p659/r13.speaker: القرظي
DURR-FULL:v7p659/r13.claim: Al-Qurazi says Abraham fulfilled his duty by sacrificing his son.
DURR-FULL:v7p659/r13.anchor: عن القرظي {وإبراهيم الذي وفى} قال: وفى بذبح ابنه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130/r2.claim: The ten Abrahamic scrolls are estimated at ten sheets in old script, about four Qur'anic verses per sheet, or forty verses total.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130/r2.anchor: وقدرت بعشر صحف ، أي مقدار عشر ورقات بالخط القديم ، تسع الورقة قرابة أربع آيات من آي القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130/r3.claim: In the earlier-scriptures passage Abraham precedes Moses because he was earlier, while here Moses is first for the greater extent of his scriptures.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130/r3.anchor: وإنما قدم في سورة الأعلى صحف إبراهيم على صحف موسى مراعاة لوقوعهما بدلا من الصحف الأولى فقدم في الذكر أقدمهما .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130/r4.claim: The author proposes that Abraham's scrolls are the words with which God tested him, and that his completing them meant conveying them to his people and believers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130/r4.anchor: وعندي أن تأخير ذكر صحف إبراهيم ليقع ما بعدها هنا جامعا لما احتوت عليه صحف إبراهيم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130/r5.claim: The author links Abraham's fulfillment to the testing words in 2:124 and his fulfillment of the dream in 37:105.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130/r5.anchor: منها ما في قوله تعالى : { وإذ ابتلى إبراهيم ربه بكلمات فأتمهن }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130/r6.claim: Calling Abraham one who fulfilled indicts the pagans: he transmitted revelation to his people and descendants, but Arabs abandoned it for idolatry.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130/r6.anchor: ووصف إبراهيم بذلك تسجيل على المشركين بأن إبراهيم بلغ ما أوحي إليه إلى قومه وذريته ولكن العرب أهملوا ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r4.claim: Before Abraham, an ally could be held for a killing; Abraham fulfilled and conveyed the rule that no bearer carries another’s burden.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r4.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: كانوا قبل إبراهيم يأخذون الولي بالولي في القتل ونحوه فوفى إبراهيم وبلغ هذا الحكم من أنه لا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس والربيع
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r5.claim: They say Abraham fulfilled God’s command to sacrifice his son.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا والربيع: وفى طاعة الله في أمر ذبح ابنه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r6.speaker: الحسن وابن جبير وقتادة وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r6.claim: They say Abraham fulfilled his mission in conveying the message and was true to his Lord.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r6.anchor:
وقال الحسن وابن جبير وقتادة وغيره، وفى
تبليغ رسالته والظاهر في ذات ربه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r7.speaker: عكرمة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r7.claim: ʿIkrima says Abraham fulfilled these ten verses, beginning with ألا تزر.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r7.anchor: وقال عكرمة، وفي هذه العشر الآيات، ألا تزر وما بعدها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r8.claim: They say Abraham perfectly performed all worship and the branches of faith and Islam, receiving release from Hell.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r8.anchor: وفى ما افترض عليه من الطاعات على وجهها وتكلمت له شعب الإيمان والإسلام فأعطاه الله براءته من النار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Abraham fulfilled thirty shares of Islamic law.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r9.anchor: قال ابن عباس: وفي شرائع الإسلام ثلاثين سهما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r10.speaker: أبو أمامة عن النبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r10.claim: Abū Umāma attributes to the Prophet that Abraham fulfilled four prayers daily.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r10.anchor: وقال أبو أمامة ورفعه إلى النبي عليه السلام وفى أربع صلوات في كل يوم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r11.claim: The strongest view is that Abraham completed all acts of worship constituting Islam; only Abraham and Muḥammad completed the religion, as when Abraham completed God’s trials.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r11.anchor: والأقوى من هذه الأقوال كلها القول العام لجميع الطاعات المستوفية لدين الإسلام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r12.speaker: ابن جبير وأبو مالك وابن السميفع
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r12.claim: They read وفى with a light fāʾ; the explanations of what he fulfilled remain the same.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r12.anchor: وقرأ ابن جبير وأبو مالك وابن السميفع: «وفى» مخففة الفاء، والخلاف فيما وفى به كالخلاف فيما وفاه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r13.speaker: النبي وأبو أمامة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r13.claim: The light-fāʾ reading is also transmitted from the Prophet and read by Abū Umāma.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r13.anchor: ورويت القراءة عن النبي عليه السلام، وقرأها أبو أمامة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463#2/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير والثوري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463#2/r1.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Thawri say Ibrahim fulfilled all that he was commanded.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463#2/r1.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير، والثوري أي بلغ جميع ما أمر به.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that Ibrahim fulfilled his duty to God by conveying the message.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463#2/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir endorses Qatada's broad reading, also chosen by Ibn Jarir: Ibrahim obeyed, delivered his message fully, fulfilled every command, and became an exemplar; 2:124 and 16:123 support this.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463#2/r3.anchor: وقال قتادة: {وفى} طاعة الله، وأدى رسالته إلى خلقه. وهذا القول هو اختيار ابن جرير، وهو يشمل الذي قبله، ويشهد له قوله تعالى:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463#2/r4.speaker: أبو أمامة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463#2/r4.claim: A report from the Prophet says Ibrahim's fulfillment was completing four units of prayer at the start of the day; Ibn Kathir calls its chain weak because it comes through Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463#2/r4.anchor: عن أبي أمامة قال: تلا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم هذه الآية: {وإبراهيم الذي وفى} قال: "أتدري ما وفى؟

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463#2/r5.speaker: أبو الدرداء وأبو ذر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الله عز وجل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463#2/r5.claim: A sacred hadith says: Adam's child, bow to Me for four units early in the day and I will suffice you for its remainder.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463#2/r5.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء وأبي ذر، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الله، عز وجل، أنه قال: "ابن آدم اركع لي أربع ركعات

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463#2/r6.speaker: معاذ بن أنس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463#2/r6.claim: A report says God named Ibrahim His intimate friend who fulfilled because he recited 30:17 each morning and evening to the end of the verse; Ibn Jarir also transmits it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463#2/r6.anchor: عن سهل بن معاذ بن أنس، عن أبيه، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: "ألا أخبركم لم سمى الله إبراهيم خليله

JISHUMI:v9p6660/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6660/r4.speaker: قراءة العامة
JISHUMI:v9p6660/r4.claim: The common reading has waffā with shadda, meaning Abraham fulfilled completely.
JISHUMI:v9p6660/r4.anchor: قراءة العامة: وفى بالتشديد، وعن سعيد بن جبير: وفى بالتخفيف

JISHUMI:v9p6660/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6660/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
JISHUMI:v9p6660/r5.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr reads lightly, meaning Abraham fulfilled what he promised and covenanted.
JISHUMI:v9p6660/r5.anchor: وعن سعيد بن جبير: وفى بالتخفيف

JISHUMI:v9p6660/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6660/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6660/r6.claim: Tawfiya means giving something in full; wafā means fulfilling one's due completely.
JISHUMI:v9p6660/r6.anchor: التوفية: إعطاء الشيء على التمام، وفى حقه توفية

JISHUMI:v9p6661/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وقتادة وابن زيد
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r2.claim: One explanation says Abraham fully carried out God's commands by delivering his message and explaining its laws.
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r2.anchor: قيل: فعل ما أمره الله على التمام من تبليغ رسالته، وبيان شرائعه، عن سعيد بن جبير، وقتادة، وابن زيد

JISHUMI:v9p6661/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r3.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r3.claim: Another explanation says Abraham fulfilled his trials: sacrifice of his son, the fire, and harm from his people.
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r3.anchor: وقيل: امتحن بذبح ولده، وإلقائه في النار، وتحمل الأذى من قومه

JISHUMI:v9p6661/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r4.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid say Abraham fulfilled his task by conveying that no bearer bears another's burden; Ibn ʿAbbās says he prohibited an earlier custom of transferring sins among kin and neighbors.
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r4.anchor: وقيل: وفى في تبليغ الرسالة التي هي قوله: ألا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى، عن ابن عباس، ومجاهد

JISHUMI:v9p6661/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r5.speaker: الحسن وسعيد بن جبير وقتادة وابن زيد
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r5.claim: These authorities say Abraham endured and conveyed what he was commanded.
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r5.anchor: وقيل: تحمل ما أمر به وبلغ، عن الحسن، وسعيد بن جبير، وقتادة، وابن زيد

JISHUMI:v9p6661/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r6.speaker: مجاهد
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r6.claim: Mujāhid says Abraham fulfilled everything imposed on him.
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r6.anchor: وقيل: وفى بما فرض عليه، عن مجاهد

JISHUMI:v9p6661/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r7.speaker: الربيع
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r7.claim: Al-Rabīʿ says Abraham fulfilled his vision by proceeding to sacrifice his son.
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r7.anchor: وقيل: وفى رؤياه، وقام بذبح ابنه، عن الربيع

JISHUMI:v9p6661/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r8.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r8.claim: Another view identifies Abraham's fulfillment with Islamic law, citing God's trial of Abraham.
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r8.anchor: وقيل: شرائع الإسلام، وهي قوله: (وإذ ابتلى إبراهيم ربه بكلمات)

JISHUMI:v9p6661/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r9.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r9.claim: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna says Abraham fulfilled the trust.
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r9.anchor: وقيل: أدى الأمانة، عن سفيان بن عيينة

JISHUMI:v9p6661/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r10.speaker: الضحاك
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r10.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says Abraham fulfilled the rites of pilgrimage.
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r10.anchor: وقيل: وفى أمور المناسك، عن الضحاك

JISHUMI:v9p6661/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r11.speaker: عطاء بن السائب
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r11.claim: A report says Abraham vowed never to ask anyone for anything; when Gabriel offered help as he was thrown into the fire, Abraham declined and fulfilled his vow.
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r11.anchor: وقيل: كان حلف لا يسأل مخلوقا شيئا، فلما قذف في النار، أتاه جبريل، وقال: ألك حاجة؟

JISHUMI:v9p6661/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r12.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r12.claim: Another view says Abraham fulfilled his profession of submission, proving faithful through tests of wealth, self, and child.
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r12.anchor: وقيل: قام بشرط ما ادعى؛ لأنه قال: أسلمت، فابتلي في ماله ونفسه وولده

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427/r5.claim: وفى is read light or doubled; doubling intensifies fulfillment or means fully completed.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427/r5.anchor: قرىء مخففا ومشددا ، والتشديد مبالغة في الوفاء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427/r6.claim: Its general wording covers conveying the message, carrying prophetic burdens, enduring the intended sacrifice and Nimrod's fire, and serving guests personally.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427/r6.anchor: وإطلاقه ليتناول كل وفاء وتوفية ، من ذلك : تبليغه الرسالة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427/r7.speaker: الحسن
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427/r7.claim: Al-Hasan said Abraham fulfilled every command from God.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427/r7.anchor: وعن الحسن : ما أمره الله بشيء إلا وفى به

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427/r8.speaker: الهذيل بن شرحبيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427/r8.claim: Al-Hudhayl says people between Noah and Abraham bore others' crimes; Abraham first opposed this.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427/r8.anchor: بين نوح وبين إبراهيم يؤخذ الرجل بجريرة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427/r9.speaker: عطاء بن السائب
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427/r9.claim: Ata ibn al-Saib says Abraham vowed never to ask a created being; in the fire he told Gabriel and Michael he had no need of them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427/r9.anchor: وعن عطاء بن السائب : عهد أن لا يسأل مخلوقا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427/r10.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427/r10.claim: The Prophet said Abraham fulfilled his work with four rakas each day in the early morning, the Duha prayer.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427/r10.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 1105 ) وفى عمله كل يوم بأربع ركعات

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427#2/r1.claim: A report asks why God called Abraham His intimate friend the one who fulfilled; he recited morning and evening glorifications from 30:17–18.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427#2/r1.anchor: ألا أخبركم لم سمى الله خليله { الذى وفى } ؟ كان يقول

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427#2/r2.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427#2/r2.claim: Another explanation says Abraham fulfilled thirty shares of Islam, ten each from the Repentance, Ahzab, and Believers passages.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427#2/r2.anchor: وقيل : وفي سهام الإسلام : وهي ثلاثون : عشرة في التوبة

MUQATIL:53:33-42/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:53:33-42/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:53:33-42/r5.claim: Abraham fulfilled his duty to God by conveying to his people what God commanded him.
MUQATIL:53:33-42/r5.anchor: لله بالبلاغ، وبلغ قومه ما أمره الله تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وقتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r4.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr and Qatada read waffā with a light f, meaning truthful in word and deed; the doubled-f reading means completing every duty.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r4.anchor: وقرأ سعيد بن جبير وقتادة «وفى» خفيفة ومعناها صدق في قوله

QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r5.claim: The doubled-f reading means Abraham completed all that was prescribed without omission; tawfiya means completion.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r5.anchor: أي قام بجميع ما فرض عليه فلم يخرم منه شيئا

QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r6.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r6.claim: Al-Warraq says Abraham fulfilled his claim of submission; God tested him in wealth, child, and self and found him true.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r6.anchor: وقال أبو بكر الوراق: قام بشرط ما ادعى وذلك أن الله تعالى قال له:

QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r7.speaker: الهيثم عن أبي أمامة عن النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r7.claim: A report says Abraham fulfilled by performing four rakʿas at the beginning of each day.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r7.anchor: وقيل: وفي عمله كل يوم بأربع ركعات في صدر النهار رواه الهيثم

QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r8.speaker: سهل بن سعد الساعدي عن أبيه
QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r8.claim: A report from the Prophet explains Abraham's epithet by his morning and evening glorification.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r8.anchor: وروى سهل بن سعد الساعدي عن أبيه:

QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r9.speaker: سهل بن معاذ عن أنس عن أبيه عن النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r9.claim: The same explanation is also transmitted by Sahl ibn Muʿadh from Anas, his father, and the Prophet.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r9.anchor: ورواه سهل بن معاذ عن أنس عن أبيه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r11.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وسعيد بن جبير ومجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r11.claim: They say Abraham did what he was commanded and conveyed God's messages; al-Qurtubi prefers this general interpretation.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r11.anchor: وقال الحسن وقتادة وسعيد بن جبير في قوله تعالى «وفى»
